findings.claim: fenceRun accepts a line as a fence under rules looser than CommonMark. It allows any indent, so a 4+ space indented code line holding ``` counts as a fence. It also lets a backtick fence open with backticks in the info string, so inline code such as "```x``` text" opens a fence. A spurious unclosed fence hides every later "## " heading, including "## Log" and "## Tasks". The document then parses with missing sections where it parsed correctly before, so the shaper-entry guard can wrongly block or allow a task. The commit message says "any indent" and the test asserts a 4-space fence, so this is deliberate, but it is a new false-positive path.

Fence state is tracked across the whole document, not just the Log. An unclosed fence anywhere earlier, such as in Specs, silently swallows the ## Tasks and ## Log headings, with no diagnostic. Before this change such a document parsed fine.

evidence: Reviewed the diff only: fenceRun's fence-detection rules and the fence state machine in ParseDocument.
The new tests cover close-with-info-string and longer-closing-fence cases, but not inline triple backticks, 4+ space indent as code, or an unclosed fence.
